correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the strict insertion test: adding the absent pair changes S=sum d_i^2 by 2(D+1) and m to m+1, so increase is equivalent (m>0) to D>1+2W/m+1/m+W/m^2. D is Binomial(2n-4,p_n) after conditioning; W/m tends to c. Expanding W-cm in centered edge indicators gives orthogonal linear and quadratic parts, with variance/n tending to c^3/2+c^2/2 and mean/sqrt(n) to c beta/2. For each fixed cumulant of order j>=3, only edge-overlap-connected motif tuples survive; each union has e>=v-1 and joint-cumulant bound O(p_n^e) by the partition formula, giving O(n) in total. This establishes the stated normal limit by moments. Deleting the two endpoints costs O_P(1) edges and O_P(1) wedges (the wedge expectation is bounded), and leaves a background independent of D. On the sole critical atom D=2c+1 the inequality is W-cm<-(m+W)/(2m); the scaled correction tends to zero, and the continuous Gaussian sign test gives Phi(-beta/sqrt(2(1+c))). The Poisson atom counts, beta=0 midpoint and c=1 values agree. The m=0 convention has vanishing weight. The bundled checker.py was inspected, not executed; the cumulant proof, not its finite/simulation checks, establishes the limit.
